answer: I'd like to talk about a trip that did not go to plan at all, but still turned out well. A time I had to change my plans quite suddenly was when a long-awaited trip with friends fell through at the last minute due to bad weather. The original plan was to spend three days in Cox's Bazar, but a cyclone warning was issued the day before we were due to leave, and our bus was cancelled. I had been looking forward to it for weeks, so the cancellation was initially a [[crushing disappointment]]. Rather than sulking about it, though, we decided to be flexible and [[make the best of]] the situation. We ended up organising a day trip to a char, one of the sandy river islands in the Jamuna, something none of us had planned. We hired a small boat, packed a picnic and spent the afternoon walking on the sandbanks and watching the fishermen bring in their nets. To our surprise, it turned out to be a wonderful day, arguably better than the original plan. What I took from it was that rigidity often leads to frustration, whereas being [[adaptable]] opens up unexpected opportunities. It was a good reminder that plans [[falling apart]] is not always a bad thing. Honestly, some of my best experiences have come from [[spontaneous]] changes like that, and I remember feeling surprisingly content on the boat home as the sun went down. I now try to hold my plans a little more loosely and stay open to whatever comes.

followUps.q: Did you manage to go to Cox's Bazar later?
followUps.answer: Yes, about three months later, once the weather had settled. It was lovely, but funnily enough, when we talk about that year, it is usually the day on the char that we remember.

followUps.q: Do you usually plan your trips carefully?
followUps.answer: I plan the essentials, like transport and where to stay, but I leave the rest fairly open. Too much planning makes a trip feel like work, and the unexpected moments are often the best.

note: Cox's Bazar trip cancelled by a cyclone warning, replaced by a boat trip to a Jamuna char; plain marks 'disappointment'/'flexible' upgraded to 'crushing disappointment' and 'make the best of'; added 'falling apart'.
